transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ava M., Ravi P., Jun P. (Redwood) — Maya C., Luis O., Priya N., Eliot G. (Obsidian)

Summary (auto): orientation + network sprint, KMS alignment, canary pilot plan.

[00:00] Ava: okay hi everyone thanks for joining on time we can do quick intros I'm Ava Morales from Redwood inference on the AE side and with me is Ravi our CSM and Jun SE. Hi Maya, would you like to kick off?
[00:18] Maya: yeah thanks Ava, appreciate it. Quick background from our side obisidian is building an internal agent framework for ops automation, we need a private deployment pattern that fits our compliance timeline. We're targeting a pilot in late March but open to moving a week if needed.
[00:34] Luis: hey all, I'm Luis, SRE, main concern is egress IPs and minimizing NAT complexity, want to avoid hairpinning traffic.
[00:44] Priya: Priya here, platform security — we'll need KMS integration details and audit log retention options, plus confirmation of SOC2 controls.
[00:55] Eliot: and I'm Eliot product, success metric for pilot is sub-120ms median token latency for short prompts and throughput 500-1k reqs/min for background processes.
[01:12] Jun: great, thanks, quick note Jun here. We'll probably recommend a short two-week network sprint to lock down VPC peering, allowlist and KMS patterns before we run the canary. That aligns with what we've done with similar financial customers.
[01:30] Maya: that sounds doable. can you elaborate on the dedicated pool idea? we want isolation but cost is a factor.
[01:39] Ava: sure, Dedicated (redwood dedicated) is reserved GPU pool; you can size a small pool for the canary and then expand later. the tradeoff is cost predictability versus hosted fallback which is cheaper but less isolated.
[01:57] Priya: any documentation on envelope encryption and whether we can bring our own keys?
[02:05] Jun: yes, we support BYOK via KMS/HSM integrations, envelope encryption pattern is documented — I'll share examples. quick caveat transcription note: in the doc it sometimes says K-V cash but that's a typo, it's KV cache.
[02:22] Luis: right, about egress — we want a small list of static IPs we can put in firewall rules, does Redwood provide egress IPs for private deploy?
[02:31] Ava: for Private deployments we provide NAT egress IPs for the control plane, but if you're in VPC-peering mode you can also route directly — we'll send the network checklist.
[02:45] Eliot: what about fallback? if Dedicated is saturated do you have auto-fallback to hosted models? we need graceful degradation.
[02:55] Jun: yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible model variants. we can configure policy to prefer low-latency model within the pool then fallback to hosted with rate limit shaping to avoid client errors.
[03:12] Maya: timeline question — you mentioned two-week sprint, what's the rough milestones?
[03:20] Ravi: high level: week 1 network & security (CIDRs, peering, firewall, KMS access) — deliverable: successful control-plane tunnel & test endpoint; week 2 bench & runbook (throughput tests, regression prompts, runbook handoff). by end of week 2 we aim for a canary window.
[03:40] Priya: about logs — we need audit logs to stay for 2 years, is that supported?
[03:46] Jun: yes audit logs are configurable retention on Private and Dedicated — for hosted API there's a different retention default, but enterprise add-on can increase retention. we'll attach the policy matrix.
[03:59] Maya: good. any network specifics — ports and DNS?
[04:05] Jun: minimal: outbound TCP 443 to control plane, ephemeral ports for data plane, DNS resolution to *.redwood-inference.svc. sample terraform snippets will clarify.
[04:20] Luis: can you confirm we don't need to open 22? we have strict bastion rules.
[04:25] Ava: no need to open 22; management plane is via API and control-plane connectivity — SSH not required.
[04:33] Eliot: on the pilot metrics, median latency target is 120ms, p95 under 300ms for short prompts. can we get telemetry to graph token-level latency?
[04:45] Ravi: console provides token-level breakdowns per route and model, we'll make sure you have access to the route-level dashboards.
[04:54] Maya: what's the suggested prompt set size for the bench test?
[04:58] Jun: 100-200 prompts representing common calls, plus synthetic high-throughput load to exercise batching and KV cache warmup. we'll include a sample prompt set.
[05:12] Priya: question on key rotation — if we rotate keys monthly how does that affect in-flight requests?
[05:19] Jun: typical pattern is key-rotation with envelope keys, we support key versioning to avoid breaking in-flight decryption; we'll provide diagram.
[05:29] Speaker 7: (inaudible)
[05:33] Ava: ok moving on, operations & runbook — Ravi will own the runbook template. Ravi, can you give quick outline?
[05:41] Ravi: yes, runbook will include: pre-launch checklist, failover steps, rollback to hosted, alerting thresholds, postmortem template and contact matrix. we'll make it prescriptive so your on-call can follow.
[05:55] Luis: we want explicit steps for DNS failover if peering goes down, and how to re-route to hosted.
[06:02] Ravi: noted, that'll be in the rollback section with exact API calls and firewall changes.
[06:09] Maya: stakeholders — who needs to be involved from Redwood during the sprint?
[06:13] Ava: typically AE, CSM, SE and an infra on-call. Jun will be primary SE. we'll invite infra eng and a solutions architect if deep tuning is required.
[06:26] Eliot: procurement / legal — any standard MSA we should expect?
[06:31] Ava: yes our standard enterprise MSA + DPA; we can provide the draft contract and security questionnaire for redlines.
[06:38] Priya: please include specifics on data residency and encryption-at-rest policy.
[06:43] Jun: will do. quick aside — some customers have integrated their KMS via a sidecar; others used cloud provider KMS direct. we can discuss pros/cons after we see your KMS provider.
[06:58] Maya: we're on HashiCorp Vault for now.
[07:01] Jun: perfect, we've onboarded Vault before; sample config will help.
[07:06] Ava: logistics — can we lock a bench test window? Jun, what do you need from Obsidian?
[07:12] Jun: need CIDRs, egress IPs, sample prompt set, and a 2-hour window with infra on-call. also indicate expected concurrency pattern.
[07:22] Luis: we can do Friday 2026-03-19 09:00-11:00 PST if that works.
[07:29] Jun: that works on our side, penciled in.
[07:33] Maya: few risk items: 1) KMS approvals can take time internally — Priya please own that timeline; 2) procurement review of MSA — we may need legal touchpoints.
[07:45] Priya: taking ownership of KMS, I'll start the security intake and get internal sign-off.
[07:50] Ava: sounds good. any other blockers?
[07:53] Eliot: cost estimates — can you send a small pilot cost table (est per hour of a small dedicated node) and a rough forecast for scaling?
[08:01] Ava: yes we'll send a tailored cost sheet. note quantization and batching settings can reduce cost — Jun will include recommended profiles per workload.
[08:12] Jun: on quantization: for background batch jobs we often suggest int8 profiles, for latency-sensitive chat keep fp16 or int4 with tuned kernels — all depends on acceptable quality delta.
[08:28] Luis: noted. also, do you provide SOC2/ISO certs? Priya asked earlier.
[08:33] Ava: yes SOC2 Type II available, ISO in process — we'll attach the certs to the security questionnaire.
[08:40] Maya: okay if we map next steps — send network checklist by Thursday, KMS Qs answered by next Monday.
[08:48] Ava: yes we'll do that. I'll share a Confluence link with artifacts: network-checklist.md, sample-terraform.tf, bench-prompt-set.json, runbook-template.md.
[08:58] Priya: will you also include the data-flow diagram for envelope encryption?
[09:02] Jun: yep.
[09:05] Ethan: (voice off)
[09:08] Maya: last question — are there guardrails for rate-limiting during canary to protect the production pool?
[09:15] Jun: you can set route-based rate limits and token quotas; we'll propose conservative quotas for canary.
[09:24] Ava: ok let's recap real quick: action items assigned, bench test Friday 03/19 09-11 PST, Redwood sends network checklist & cost sheet by 03/12, Jun to schedule bench and share prompt set, Priya to provide KMS contact by 03/14, Ravi to draft runbook by 03/16.
[09:45] Maya: agreed. thanks everyone.
[09:48] Luis: thanks.
[09:50] Ava: thanks, we'll follow up in email with next steps and links.
[56:30] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains a few inaudible segments and auto-captions errors (e.g., K-V cash instead of KV cache). Links referenced during call: https://redwood.example.com/network-checklist (placeholder), bench-prompt-set link to drive (placeholder).
